ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an 11 V rectangular pulse of duration 10 μs applied between the left input terminals. The upper input terminal feeds a 1 kΩ series resistor. After this resistor, the node is connected to a 10 kΩ resistor down to the lower reference node, and an 11 nF capacitor is connected in parallel with that 10 kΩ resistor to the same lower reference node. Reasoning: During the high portion of the pulse, the capacitor sees the source and resistors through their Thevenin equivalent. The Thevenin voltage at the capacitor node is the divider voltage across the 10 kΩ resistor: Vth = 11 V × 10 kΩ / (1 kΩ + 10 kΩ) = 10 V. With the ideal pulse source shorted for Thevenin resistance, Rth = 1 kΩ || 10 kΩ = (1×10)/(1+10) kΩ = 0.909 kΩ = 909 Ω. The time constant is τ = Rth C = 909 Ω × 11 nF ≈ 10 μs. Since the capacitor is initially discharged, vC(t) = Vth(1 − e^(−t/τ)). At t = 10 μs, vC = 10(1 − e^(−1)) ≈ 6.32 V. This is the peak value reached at the end of the pulse.

Since the voltage rises monotonically during the pulse, this endpoint value is the peak.
